takes.p: All three Terrifier films (2016, 2022 and 2024) are back in theaters on consecutive nights around Halloween, presented by Dead by Daylight ahead of Art the Clown's arrival in the game, Rue Morgue reports.

The National Science and Media Museum in Bradford holds the Ashton & Leakey Collection: sketches, prosthetics, glass eyes and fangs from Hammer make-up artists Roy Ashton and Phil Leakey, covering The Curse of Frankenstein (1957), Dracula (1958), The Mummy (1959) and The Gorgon (1964). Great British Life reports the museum is opening the collection up.

takes.h: Smile and A Quiet Place join the Hellbreak card game
takes.p: Monsters from Smile, Sleepy Hollow and A Quiet Place are joining Spin Master's Hellbreak trading card game, Rue Morgue reports. The game was built with Universal; its first reveals were Count Dracula, the Bride of Frankenstein and the shark from Jaws.

takes.h: Kurosawa and Shimizu direct Disney+'s Night Tales Club
takes.p: Night Tales Club, a six-part Disney+ anthology adapted from stories by Ichi Sawamura, premieres in January 2027. Kiyoshi Kurosawa, Takashi Shimizu and Shinzo Katayama are among the six episode directors; Takayuki Yamada stars in the framing story as a wealthy man who pays for accounts of the unexplained.

Hammer's Limited Collector's Edition of Dracula (1958) was scheduled for October 26, Dread Central reported: seven discs (two 4K UHD, five Blu-ray) carrying five versions of the film, including the uncensored UK cut rebuilt from Japanese reels found in Warner Bros.' archive, plus a 200-page book and a 60-page House of Hammer comic reprint.

takes.h: Ryū Murakami, author of Audition, dies at 74
takes.p: Rue Morgue reports that Ryū Murakami, author of Audition and In the Miso Soup, has died at 74. No cause was given. Audition (1997) became Takashi Miike's 1999 film.

takes.h: Tom Skerritt, Captain Dallas of Alien, dies at 93
takes.p: Rue Morgue reports that Tom Skerritt, who played Captain Dallas in Alien (1979), has died at 93. His other genre credits include The Dead Zone (1983), Poltergeist III (1988) and the TV film Stephen King's Desperation (2006).
